time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk data summarized from Svantesson 1985
claim: Non-high rounded vowels are restricted to initial syllables in Kalmyk. The non-high front e/ö and back a/o rounding contrasts are neutralized post-initially, where non-high vowels are unrounded; the restriction extends throughout the word and excludes non-high rounded vowels from suffixes.
normalized_environment: NONHIGH_ROUNDED allowed only INITIAL_SYLLABLE; ROUNDING contrast neutralized POSTINITIAL
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Kaun reports no evidence of labial attraction in Kalmyk; this positional neutralization is not productive rounding harmony.

time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk data summarized from Svantesson 1985
claim: Kalmyk suffix vocalism has only two contrastive height degrees: high rounded suffix vowels alternate u/ü by harmony class, low unrounded suffix vowels alternate back/front, and invariant high unrounded i also occurs. The mid front vowel e never appears in suffixes despite being allowed as a front-harmonic vowel elsewhere.

suffix_classes.low_unrounded: A = back a / front low vowel (source PDF extraction renders the front vowel as ú)

normalized_environment: SUFFIX_VOWEL inventory = LOW_UNROUNDED harmonic pair + HIGH_ROUNDED harmonic pair + invariant i; e absent
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The absence of non-high rounded vowels follows the broader postinitial restriction; Kaun explicitly notes that the absence of e does not follow from that rounding-based explanation.

time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk data summarized from Svantesson 1985
claim: The causative suffix has a high rounded back/front alternation: -u:l after back-harmonic stems versus -ü:l after front-harmonic stems.
normalized_environment: CAUSATIVE.V = u if BACK_HARMONIC; ü if FRONT_HARMONIC
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This is front/back harmony, not rounding harmony; both allomorphs are high rounded.

time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk data summarized from Svantesson 1985
claim: Kaun qualifies the common description of /i/ as neutral: in Svantesson's data there are no examples with /i/ flanked by back vowels, so the only directly demonstrated neutral context is suffixal /i/. Many historical medial /i/ tokens have been lost in modern Kalmyk, reducing the evidence base for transparency within roots.

source_forms.reported_gap: no Svantesson forms with i flanked by back vowels
source_forms.diachrony: many original medial i tokens lost

formal_environment: BACK_V ... i ... BACK_V versus suffix i
normalized_environment: ROOT_INTERNAL_i transparency underdetermined in cited corpus; SUFFIX_i neutrality demonstrated
scope: Svantesson 1985 Kalmyk dataset as audited by Kaun
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Do not recode /i/ as fully transparent in every position from this evidence; Kaun explicitly calls the characterization analytically problematic.

time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk with Classical Mongolian comparison
claim: A historical sequence corresponding to Classical Mongolian morpheme-final /ai/ yields long /a:/ in Kalmyk; Kaun explicitly treats this as monophthongization with compensatory lengthening and gives both bare and suffixed examples.
normalized_environment: DIACHRONIC MONOPHTHONGIZATION ai > a: with compensatory lengthening
scope: Kalmyk reflexes of Classical Mongolian forms
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This is diachronic evidence and should not be treated as a productive synchronic phonotactic repair without independent evidence.
